findings.locator: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 71–73; textual-removal allegation and dialogue
findings.document_finding: Justin accuses some Jewish teachers of omissions from the Septuagint and Trypho asks which scriptures were allegedly removed.
findings.claim_examined: Justin even acknowledges that the Jeremiah passage he disputes was still present in some synagogue copies. The diversity of ancient witnesses—including those associated with the Dead Sea Scrolls—must be evaluated passage by passage.
findings.qualification: A contested early Christian allegation is not independent proof of systematic deliberate alteration by later Jewish communities. findings.locator: Trent Session IV decree on sacred books and traditions (8 April 1546)
findings.document_finding: The council expressly receives written books, provides an enumerated canon and mentions unwritten apostolic traditions.
findings.claim_examined: An inspired book does not cease to be Scripture because a later confessional community rejects it. The Church receives, preserves and authoritatively identifies the biblical canon as part of the apostolic deposit; Trent safeguarded this received collection amid disputes.
findings.qualification: Trent's decree cannot by itself establish unanimous second-century recognition of every listed book. Source relevance is being cross-checked against an additional claim in this same canonical dossier; other propositions and French wording remain independently unapproved.
